content: 1. Cabotegravir and rilpivirine are available as extended-release injectable suspensions. 2. The use of rifampin is contraindicated as it increases the metabolism of cabotegravir, leading to reduced drug levels and efficacy. 3. Cabotegravir is metabolized by UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 enzymes. Strong inducers of these enzymes can decrease systemic exposure to cabotegravir, potentially resulting in virologic failure. 4. Testosterone is contraindicated as it increases the metabolism of cabotegravir, reducing its levels and effectiveness. 5. Close monitoring is required when using ublituximab, as its immunosuppressive effects may reduce the efficacy of cabotegravir and increase the risk of infections. 6. Zinc can decrease the absorption of cabotegravir in the gastrointestinal tract due to cation binding. Therapy should be modified, and zinc-containing products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after oral cabotegravir. 7. Hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema and urticaria, have been reported with cabotegravir. 8. Hepatotoxicity has been observed in patients with or without pre-existing liver disease or risk factors. Liver function tests should be monitored, and treatment should be discontinued if hepatotoxicity is suspected. 9. Depressive disorders, including suicidal ideation and attempts, have been reported, particularly in individuals with a history of depression or psychiatric illness. Patients should be promptly evaluated if symptoms emerge, and the risks and benefits of continued therapy should be assessed. 10. Co-administration with UGT1A1 inducers such as carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampin, and rifapentine is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure. 11. For HIV-1 treatment, cabotegravir oral therapy should not be initiated in combination with rifabutin. 12. For HIV-1 PrEP, individuals with unknown or positive HIV-1 status should not use cabotegravir. 13. Hepatotoxicity has been reported in patients with or without pre-existing liver conditions. Liver chemistries should be monitored, and treatment should be discontinued if liver toxicity is suspected. 14. Depressive disorders, including mood changes, suicidal ideation, and suicide attempts, have been reported. Patients should be evaluated promptly if symptoms arise, and the risks and benefits of therapy should be reassessed. 15. When used with rilpivirine, consider the contraindications, precautions, and drug interactions associated with rilpivirine. 16. Healthcare providers are encouraged to register pregnant patients in the Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry (APR) by calling 1-800-258-4263. The rate of miscarriage is not reported in the APR, and the background risk for major birth defects and miscarriage in the indicated population is unknown. 17. Data on the use of cabotegravir during pregnancy are insufficient to assess the risk of birth defects and miscarriage. Healthcare providers should discuss the benefits and risks of using the drug with individuals of childbearing potential or during pregnancy. 18. It is unknown if cabotegravir is present in human breast milk, affects milk production, or impacts breastfed infants. 19. HIV-1–infected mothers receiving cabotegravir should not breastfeed due to the risk of HIV-1 transmission, viral resistance, and adverse reactions in the infant. 20. Detectable cabotegravir concentrations may persist in systemic circulation for up to 12 months or longer after discontinuing intramuscular injections. Breastfeeding should only occur if the benefits outweigh the potential risks to the infant. 21. For uninfected mothers receiving cabotegravir for HIV-1 PrEP, the benefit-risk of the drug to the infant while breastfeeding should be assessed. 22. Mothers with suspected acute HIV-1 infection should not breastfeed due to the risk of HIV-1 transmission to the infant. 23. Cabotegravir is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 24. The drug is excreted in urine (27%) and feces (59%, with 47% unchanged). 25. Cabotegravir should be taken on a regular dosing schedule with a meal at the same time as rilpivirine. 26. If a dose is missed, it should be taken as soon as remembered. 27. Patients should not stop taking cabotegravir or run out of the medication due to the risk of viral resistance. 28. If the medication is stored in a refrigerator, it should be brought to room temperature before administration (not exceeding 30°C or 86°F). 29. The vial should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. If either is observed, the vial should be discarded. 30. The vial should be shaken vigorously to ensure the suspension is uniform before injection. Small air bubbles are expected and acceptable. 31. Once the suspension is drawn into a syringe, it should be administered as soon as possible but may remain in the syringe for up to 2 hours. 32. A filled syringe should not be refrigerated and should be discarded if not administered within 2 hours. 33. Cabotegravir should not be mixed with any other product or diluent. 34. The individual’s BMI should be considered to ensure the needle length is sufficient to reach the gluteal muscle. Longer needle lengths (not included in the dosing kit) may be required for individuals with a BMI >30 kg/m² to ensure intramuscular (IM) administration rather than subcutaneous (SC) injection. 35. Cabotegravir should be administered as a single IM injection in the gluteal muscle by a healthcare provider every 2 months. 36. The injection may be administered up to 7 days before or after the scheduled date. 37. Tablets should be stored below 30°C (86°F). 38. Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class. 39. Formulary information may vary and change over time. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information. 40. The recipient of this information will receive further details and instructions to access the offer.
